beliefs.label: Earn Trust
beliefs.statement: I earn trust by saying what I can actually deliver.

receipts.quote: I told Mara the new shelf signs would be ready Thursday, not Tuesday. On Thursday morning I carried the printed stack to her desk.
My daughter asked whether I could make her recital, and I checked the calendar before answering. I said yes and arrived before the lights dimmed.

beliefs.label: Do Better
beliefs.statement: I do better work when I let someone see the unfinished version.

receipts.quote: I showed Mara the half-finished member map with three empty boxes still on it. She pointed out a simpler route for the pickup arrows.
Before polishing the poster, I sent its rough layout to Jada. Her note about the tiny price type saved me from redoing the whole thing.

beliefs.label: Steady Father
beliefs.statement: I can be a steady father without making every hour productive.

receipts.quote: On Saturday my daughter and I spent an hour building a crooked birdhouse from a kit. I did not turn it into a lesson or check my phone.
My daughter wanted to replay an old puzzle game after dinner. I sat beside her until she solved the last level.

beliefs.label: Turn Vague
beliefs.statement: I turn a vague brief into pictures before I can think clearly.

receipts.quote: The co-op asked for a spring campaign, so I covered the table with thumbnail sketches before writing a headline. The right idea appeared after the fifth page.
Mara described a confusing checkout sign, and I drew three arrows on scrap paper. Once I saw the arrows, I knew where the wording belonged.

beliefs.label: Hear Criticism
beliefs.statement: I hear criticism best when it names the work rather than my character.

receipts.quote: Mara said the flyer hierarchy was hard to scan, then pointed to the crowded middle. I could revise it without feeling she had dismissed me.
My daughter said the poster's tiny text was impossible to read from her bed. I enlarged it and thanked her.

beliefs.label: Embarrassed, Make
beliefs.statement: When I am embarrassed, I make a joke before I answer.

receipts.quote: When the printer jammed during my demo, I said it had chosen violence before explaining the backup plan. The joke came out before the useful sentence.
Mara found a typo on a sign I had approved, and I joked that the letter had escaped. Then I replaced the file.

beliefs.label: Being Expected
beliefs.statement: Being expected is a form of closeness for me.

receipts.quote: Mara saved me the window seat at the staff lunch when I was late from a delivery call. I felt less like an extra chair at the table.
My daughter texted that she had kept the last cinnamon roll for me. I ate it cold and felt remembered.

beliefs.label: Protect Friday
beliefs.statement: I protect Friday evenings for my daughter even when work is loud.

receipts.quote: A client wanted revisions at 6:30 on Friday, and I replied that I would take them Monday. My daughter and I went to her film club instead.
I closed the co-op chat before picking up my daughter at the library. We chose a mystery novel on the walk home.

shared_items.label: How I mean things
shared_items.statement: I think out loud with sketches and may sound tentative while I am deciding.

shared_items.label: What feels like care
shared_items.statement: A person saving me a seat or keeping a plan makes me feel included.

shared_items.label: How to bring something up with me
shared_items.statement: Start with the specific work or moment; I can hear a direct request.
